title: Phase 1.2H-R1 private-review-boundary assessment
description: The closed document produced by scripts/phase1_2h_r1_review_boundary_assessment.py. It exists because independent Audit B (B-09) found this round's terminal state rested on prose that could not be re-executed and did not name which frozen condition failed. The assessment reads only Azure control-plane facts from a committed evidence bundle: no sealed object, no private curator file, no prompt, no response, no case, no label. A QUALIFIES verdict would not be authorisation to review; it would only mean a qualifying backend exists.

evidence_source.description: How the control-plane facts were captured, so the assessment can be reproduced.

conditions.description: Every frozen condition, in the order it appears in the decision record. A condition is never dropped: an unassessed condition must not be able to disappear silently, because absence would read as satisfaction.

verdict.description: NOT_ASSESSABLE is not a pass. It records that the property belongs to a review design that has not been provisioned and evidenced to this assessor, so the assessed inputs contain nothing to assess it against. It is scoped to those inputs and is not a claim that no such design exists anywhere.

basis.description: What was observed. Never what was hoped.

qualification_verdict.description: QUALIFIES requires every condition to PASS. Any FAIL or NOT_ASSESSABLE yields DOES_NOT_QUALIFY.

terminal_state.description: Precedence, per independent Audit B (B-09): a failed byte-only gate blocks on source access, because the boundary question has not yet been reached. Only a passed gate can be followed by a boundary block.

byte_only_gate_evidence.description: The receipt the gate outcome was derived from. Audit C (C-01): byte_only_gate_passed was formerly an operator-supplied CLI flag, so an assessment could name a terminal state its evidence did not support. It is now computed from this receipt, and the receipt is identified here by content digest so the derivation is auditable.

receipt_path.description: Repository-relative path to the receipt, or null when no gate was run.

receipt_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the receipt's raw bytes, or null when no gate was run.

passed.description: True only if every conjunct in GATE_REQUIREMENTS held. Must equal the top-level byte_only_gate_passed.

unmet_requirements.description: Every requirement the receipt failed. Empty if and only if passed is true.

platform_attested_execution.description: The Azure Container Apps execution name that the committed platform execution inventory records as Succeeded, running the image digest the receipt claims, invoked with the execution id and freeze commit the receipt claims. Null when no gate was run. Audit F (F-01): every other field here derives from a document the probe wrote about itself; this one derives from a control-plane query the probe does not author. It establishes that the receipt agrees with a separately committed transcript of the platform's execution list. It does NOT establish that the receipt's counters are true, and - as Audit F pressed on closure review - the inventory is an operator-transcribed, unsigned JSON file in this same repository, so it constrains a rogue probe and not a rogue operator. 'Attested' here names a provenance class, not cryptographic authentication.

instrument_access_effect.description: What this assessment instrument itself consumed. All pinned to zero: reading control-plane resource settings is not a semantic read, and this instrument makes no change to any resource. Audit C (C-01) note: these pins constrain what a receipt may *report*; they are not a runtime instrument. The credibility of the zeros rests on the module performing no data-plane or Azure call at all, which is checkable by reading it.
